_schema: Vegetation gib-segmentation joint-height manifest (Caleb's ruling 2026-08-05: 'take an existing tree and fragment more parts of it, essentially a gib factor for trees, high mid and low level separations'). Sibling GLBs '<species>_low.glb' / '_mid.glb' / '_high.glb' live next to the original '<species>.glb' in this same directory - the original is BYTE-IDENTICAL and untouched; tree_cover_layer.gd's solid_mesh_for() contract is unaffected until a future code change wires this in (NOT done here - state-swap only per ADR-031, never fracture/RigidBody).
_units: all heights in metres, object-space Z (source mesh's own up axis, origin at ground)

_joint_contract.cut_low_m: boundary between LOW (base/lower trunk - stays standing as a snag when a blast lands above it) and MID (upper trunk).
_joint_contract.cut_high_m: boundary between MID (upper trunk) and HIGH (canopy/crown). For bushes (no trunk) both cuts are a plain height-fraction split (33%/66%) per Caleb's ruling; trunk_detected=false marks these.
_joint_contract.usage: code should pick the joint nearest a blast height along this species' own Z range [zmin_m, zmax_m], then swap the standing instance for the corresponding _low/_mid/_high GLB (or a pair, if leaving a snag) - never fracture at runtime.
